content.rule: Schema legality alone is not semantic validity. In actual drawing-completion or physical printed-pattern transformation, inspect whether marks look like intrinsic content; a competing reasonable reading with different/no valid answer fails. No universal ban on color: numerical/geometry comparisons require their own actual-wording assessment. No question edits, new text legends or relaxed human-ambiguity standards as a fix. Preserve rejected frozen evidence; any material repair needs new PNG/preset/two calls and NEW independent review.

blocking_reason.decision: fails for this exact frozen presentation
blocking_reason.annotation_only_reading: If the colors are known to be external comparison annotations and excluded from paper content, a careful human can reject D and uniquely select E by the proof above.
blocking_reason.reasonable_material_color_reading: The question asks what picture results when the two shown physical papers are placed on a black circle. Red and blue lie exactly on the boundary of the gray source paper, and green on the white source paper. They look like colored edging/ink attached to the shown pieces, with matching edging only in D. No text or visible separate annotation convention states that these particular moving-paper features vanish or may be discarded.
explicit_incompatibility: The source red 0..90 arc and blue 90..180 arc share the same top endpoint and form one continuous semicircular outer arc. Any single rigid movement, including a planar reflection, preserves their endpoint incidence and adjacency.

D red is 0..90 and blue is 180..270. These arcs are separated around the outer circle by a white quadrant and a black quadrant; they do not share an endpoint. Their closest endpoints are sqrt(2) radii apart. They cannot both be the moved edging of one intact source gray semicircle.

E is the only possible uncolored arrangement, but E has no red, blue or green outer-edge ink. In this actual E arrangement both source curved edges lie on the outside of the disk and remain exposed; no overlap is available to hide them.
A/B/C already fail the underlying paper geometry and also lack the edging. Thus the exact color-preserving reading has no matching choice, whereas the annotation-only reading has E.
blocking_reason.why_not_a_blanket_color_ban: Authorized color styling is not automatically promoted to a new numerical or geometric given. The objection here comes from the task-specific physical transformation of the very objects carrying the colored boundaries and the explicit absence of a matching transformed picture. A purely relational geometry highlight need not have this problem.
blocking_reason.primary_semantics_claim_disposition: The design statement that colors are annotations and not extra physical ink constraints is an author intention outside the actual question/PNG delivered to the solver. It does not resolve the competing reasonable human reading.
blocking_reason.no_new_cut_claim: There is no new radius, interior cut, closed source subregion or extra gray paper in this new design. Color transitions at the existing arc midpoint do not draw a cut. That passes the Plane233-specific partition objection but does not settle the different paper-ink issue.
blocking_reason.basis: Actual image and complete wording plus the explicit adjacency/color-preservation calculation; not the model narratives and not a numerical cap on marks.

primary_proof_corrections.incorrect_claim: Any rigid placement of a radius1 sector inside the equal-radius disk has its circular arc centered at the disk center.
primary_proof_corrections.counterexample: Take Q={(x,y): x>=0, y>=0, x^2+y^2<=1} and translate it by (-1/4,-1/4). For r=sqrt(x^2+y^2), the translated squared distance from O is r^2-(x+y)/2+1/8 <= r^2-r/2+1/8 <= 5/8 < 1 for 0<=r<=1. This entire radius-1 quarter fits strictly inside the unit disk although its arc center is (-1/4,-1/4).
primary_proof_corrections.correction: Use the valid semicircle diameter-endpoint argument, actual boundary matching, area, D nonconvexity and the explicit E construction above. The original E answer survives.

primary_proof_corrections.qualification: D closed gray sectors can touch at the center; its interior is disconnected and the set is nonconvex. Single point contact cannot make it a rigid half-disk.

content.scope: Exact paper-edge color-preservation ambiguity; not blanket ban on appearance styling. Old source/evidence retained.
